original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: For transposition targets on arbitrary coordinate pairs in the formal M_R(F2[GL_n(F2)]) model, prove the exact cost 3t whenever the targets' coordinate graph has components of at most three vertices, for every n and R. Record exact formal minima at n = 3 for mixed swaps and a 3-cycle, and an all-pairs additivity census at n = 3, R = 2.
scope_change_reason: PR #4950 (pending) settled t swaps of one fixed coordinate pair and asked whether mixed targets admit the same per-target cut. This package answers that for transpositions whose coordinate graph has components of at most three vertices. It records where order-pattern cuts stop being tight (longer paths and stars at n = 4, and 3-cycles). It is a negative formal-model screen and does not satisfy the card's native construction gate.
bottleneck_link: Register sharing and address spectators give no saving for these coordinate-permutation targets under the rank-one coordinate-CNOT tariff. A saving needs a changed operation or tariff.
stop_rule: Stop at the component theorem, the exact n = 3 formal minima and census, and the recorded limits of pattern cuts. Do not search native operations.
author: James Reed
ai_assistance: Substantial assistance from Anthropic Claude (Claude Code, Opus 5.5).

open_questions.question: Are formal costs additive across several targets that are not transpositions in small components, for example two 3-cycles, or 3-edge transposition paths and stars?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A single target costs exactly its CNOT word length (the support lemma of pending PR #4974 plus a one-register word), but support bounds only the largest single target. Order-pattern cuts are not tight for these multi-target cases (3 of 6 for a 3-cycle, 8.33 and 8.14 of 9 at n = 4).
open_questions.first_step: Run the exact formal search for diag([c3],[c3]) at n = 3, R = 2 up to length 11, or find a cut that combines with the support argument.
